nodes.text: Welcome to the Riverlight Museum audio trail. Tap ahead when you are ready to leave the lobby arch.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: Ahead of you are three permanent halls, one family shortcut, and the main exit atrium.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: This museum is arranged as a loop, so you can circle back without losing your place in the narration.
nodes.speaker: Curator

nodes.text: The Fossil Gallery opens with low amber light and a timeline wall tracing 200 million years.
nodes.speaker: PaleoHost

nodes.text: Notice the bite marks along the jaw hinge; our conservation team left them visible to show the animal's final hunt.
nodes.speaker: PaleoHost

nodes.text: The projected footprints match the stride length of a running predator, letting visitors pace beside it.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Children usually compare their own shoe size to the fossil print here before moving on.
nodes.speaker: FamilyGuide

nodes.text: Ocean Court surrounds you with blue light, live reef audio, and the suspended whale model above the stairs.
nodes.speaker: MarineHost

nodes.text: The sixty-foot model overhead marks the midpoint of the route and points toward every exit in the building.
nodes.speaker: MarineHost

nodes.text: Behind the glass, staff grow coral fragments on ceramic stars before sending them back to the bay reef.
nodes.speaker: Conservator

nodes.text: This alcove lowers the soundtrack and dims the projections while preserving the same route information.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: The final wing mixes robotics, renewable energy, and early prototype sketches from local inventors.
nodes.speaker: InnovationHost

nodes.text: The robot arm sorts recycled parts by shape, echoing the same vision system used in the museum workshop downstairs.
nodes.speaker: InnovationHost

nodes.text: The touch table compares river current, rooftop solar, and battery storage with real data from this district.
nodes.speaker: Narrator

nodes.text: Drawer labels reveal how each prototype changed over time, from pencil sketch to patent model to public display.
nodes.speaker: Archivist

nodes.text: This shorter trail keeps the biggest objects and hands-on prompts while skipping the longest narration clips.
nodes.speaker: FamilyGuide

nodes.text: Elevators connect every hall, and the shortest loop avoids the whale stairs without skipping any major narration.
nodes.speaker: AccessibilityHost

nodes.text: From here, you can return to the lobby, continue by elevator, or finish near the gift shop corridor.
nodes.speaker: AccessibilityHost

nodes.text: You are back beneath the lobby arch, with every hall still available from this central hub.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: The cafe overlook faces the sculpture garden and lets you resume the tour from the same progress marker.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: The gift shop corridor closes the tour with postcards, field guides, and a final route map for future visits.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: You have reached the glass atrium exit; the audio tour ends as the doors open to the riverwalk.
nodes.speaker: Guide

nodes.text: The reading lounge offers field notebooks, reef surveys, and patent sketches if you want a quieter ending to the route.
nodes.speaker: Archivist
